_about: Single data source for every visual added to index.html (including the remade Figures 2.1–2.4, 3.1 and 3.2). Every number shown inside a visual must come from a value object below: {"v": value, "s": status}. Status: exact = appears verbatim in the page text; approximate = shown with the page's approximate sign; derived = calculated from page values (see "from"); axis = scale tick only, not a data value. "pos" fields only place a mark on a time axis and are never displayed. tools/embed_viz_data.py copies this file into index.html (script#viz-data); tools/check_viz.js checks it. v2: values from "BTL Đa biên – Nhóm 4" v5; status "figure label" = value printed on a figure of the report but not in its text.

visuals.label: Visual · Section 1.1.2 · Schematic
visuals.title: Each level of integration builds on the one below
visuals.aria: Schematic staircase of five levels of regional economic integration: Free Trade Area, Customs Union, Common Market, Economic Union, Economic and Monetary Union. Not a measurement.
visuals.unit: Schematic: block heights show order only, not a measured quantity. Select a level to read its description.
visuals.source: Compiled by the authors from the data in Section 1.1.2.

steps.name: Free Trade Area
steps.text: Members eliminate or reduce tariffs on goods traded among themselves; each member retains its own trade policy toward non-member countries.

steps.name: Customs Union
steps.text: Establishes a common external tariff toward non-member countries.

steps.name: Common Market
steps.text: Restrictions on the movement of capital, labor, and services are substantially reduced.

steps.name: Economic Union
steps.text: Members may coordinate policies concerning taxation, competition, government spending and employment.

steps.name: Economic and Monetary Union
steps.text: Members may adopt a common currency managed by a common central bank. The euro area is the most prominent contemporary example.

visuals.label: Visual · Section 1.2.2 · Schematic
visuals.title: The Commission proposes; the Parliament and the Council adopt
visuals.aria: Schematic of the relations stated in Section 1.2.2: the European Council defines overall political direction and priorities; the European Commission proposes legislation; the European Parliament and the Council of the European Union adopt EU legislation together; the Court of Justice of the European Union ensures EU law is interpreted and applied consistently; the European Central Bank is responsible for monetary policy in the euro area.
visuals.unit: Schematic: only the relations stated in the text of Section 1.2.2 are drawn.
visuals.source: Compiled by the authors from the data in Section 1.2.2.

visuals.label: Visual · Section 2.1.1
visuals.title: 21 of 27 member states use the euro (Bulgaria became the 21st on 1 January 2026)
visuals.aria: Twenty-seven stars, one per member state: 21 filled gold stars use the euro (Bulgaria the 21st, 1 January 2026), 6 outlined stars do not. Stars are not assigned to named countries.
visuals.unit: One star = one member state. Stars are not linked to particular countries.
notes: 6 = 27 − 21 (derived): Czechia, Denmark, Hungary, Poland, Romania and Sweden.

visuals.label: Figure 2.1 (a)
visuals.title: Intra-EU trade in goods, 2021–2025
visuals.aria: Bar chart, EUR billion: intra-EU trade in goods 3,442 in 2021, 4,253 in 2022, 4,101 in 2023, 4,025 in 2024 and 4,143 in 2025.
visuals.unit: EUR billion. Values as labelled in the report's figure.
notes: Numbered "Figure 1" in the report; renumbered Figure 2.1 here to follow Chapter 2.
2025*: the report notes that 2025 values are derived from reported shares and balance, and that vintages of earlier years differ slightly. The text gives about EUR 4.14 trillion (+2.6% on 2024).

visuals.label: Figure 2.1 (b)
visuals.title: Extra-EU trade balance in goods, 2021–2025
visuals.aria: Bar chart, EUR billion: balance of extra-EU trade in goods +55 in 2021, −435 in 2022, +41 in 2023, +147 in 2024 and +128 in 2025.
visuals.unit: EUR billion; surplus above the line, deficit below. Values as labelled in the report's figure.
notes: The report's figure also shows extra-EU export and import bars without value labels; only the labelled balances are drawn here.
2024: the figure shows +147; Table 2.3 gives a 2024 surplus of EUR 136 billion (different data vintage).

visuals.label: Visual · Section 2.2.1
visuals.title: The EU's network of new-generation agreements has widened since 2011
visuals.aria: Timeline of the eight agreements in Table 2.4: South Korea provisionally applied from 2011; Canada (CETA) provisionally applied since September 2017; Japan in force since 1 February 2019; Vietnam (EVFTA) in force since 1 August 2020; United Kingdom (TCA) applied since 1 May 2021; New Zealand in force since 1 May 2024; Mercosur signed 17 January 2026 and interim agreement provisionally applied from 1 May 2026; India negotiations concluded 27 January 2026.
visuals.unit: Dates from Table 2.4. Shape and label show the latest status reported.
visuals.source: European Commission; Sullivan & Cromwell (2026); Bundesbank (2026); DLA Piper (2026); Ebner Stolz (2026).

events.what: Negotiations concluded; signature and ratification pending

notes: South Korea: Table 2.4 gives the year only (2011); the mark is placed mid-year.

visuals.label: Visual · Section 2.2.3
visuals.title: EU climate targets: at least −55% by 2030, a proposed −90% by 2040, neutrality by 2050
visuals.aria: Index of net greenhouse-gas emissions, 1990 = 100. Targets: 45 or less in 2030 (at least 55% reduction), 10 in 2040 (90% reduction proposed by the Commission), 0 in 2050 (climate neutrality). All values except 1990 are derived from the stated percentages; these are targets, not projections.
notes: Targets, not projections; straight lines are schematic.
Derived: 2030 = 100 − 55 (at least 55%, so at most 45); 2040 = 100 − 90 (target proposed by the Commission, as stated in the report); 2050 = 0 (climate neutrality).
visuals.source: European Climate Law (2021); European Green Deal (2019); European Commission (n.d.-g).
